task_1.title: Remove runtime dependency on typing_extensions
task_1.description: The 2025.6.1 update removes xarray's runtime dependence on typing_extensions for datetime accessor imports, so environments that do not install that package can still import and use the library while preserving Self typing support for static analysis.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2025.6.1 no longer requires `typing_extensions` to be installed for normal runtime imports and use of the library, while preserving existing datetime accessor behavior and type annotation compatibility.

expectation.grounded: Importing and using xarray modules that expose the `.dt` datetime accessor, including `xarray.core.accessor_dt`, should not require a runtime import from `typing_extensions`. Any use of `Self` for type annotations should remain confined to type-checking contexts, using `typing.Self` on Python 3.11+ and `typing_extensions.Self` only where static typing on older Python versions needs it.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, users should be able to import and use the library normally without adding `typing_extensions` as a runtime dependency. Typing support should remain available to tools that analyze annotations, without changing user-visible datetime accessor behavior.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter the public behavior of the `.dt` accessor or introduce new runtime warnings or errors during normal imports. Compatibility for type annotations that rely on `Self` should be preserved across supported Python versions without making `typing_extensions` mandatory at runtime.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a dependency cleanup only: existing datetime-related APIs should behave the same, and the upgrade should reduce installation/runtime requirements rather than introduce new usage constraints.

behavior: Normal runtime import of the library's datetime accessor support no longer depends on the `typing_extensions` package being installed.
The `Self` annotation used by datetime accessor code is treated as a type-checking concern rather than a runtime import requirement.
On Python 3.11 and newer, static typing can rely on the standard-library `typing.Self`.
On older supported Python versions, static typing compatibility for `Self` is preserved without turning `typing_extensions` into a runtime dependency.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades to 2025.6.1 and imports xarray in an environment without `typing_extensions`, the import should succeed instead of failing due to a missing typing-only dependency.
When a user accesses datetime functionality through the `.dt` accessor after the upgrade, it should behave the same as before this dependency cleanup.
When the codebase is analyzed for typing, `Self` annotations should remain supported on both Python 3.11+ and older supported Python versions.
When users install the upgraded library for runtime use, they should not need to add `typing_extensions` solely to satisfy normal import-time behavior.
